text.p: Portuguese Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said on Friday that the government firmly believed the country would join the single currency in 1999.
Presenting an economic plan for the years 1998-2000, Sousa Franco said the programme was designed with the single currency in mind.
"It looks towards Portugal being amongst the founders of the third phase of economic and monetary union, something which we believe," he told a news conference.
The plan sees the budget deficit being halved by the year
2000 to 1.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) from a forecast 2.9 percent in 1997.
A deficit of three percent or under of GDP in 1997 is one of the key conditions for joining monetary union at the launch.
